name: SBC
summary: SBC develops liquid-argon bubble chambers for very small nuclear recoils, combining bubble formation with scintillation readout. A 10 kg Fermilab detector characterizes the technology. Future reactor deployments have been studied for coherent neutrino scattering, alongside a separate low-background dark-matter programme at SNOLAB.
detection_principle: A nuclear recoil can nucleate a bubble in superheated argon while also producing scintillation. Optical imaging and acoustic channels identify bubble formation; scintillation adds energy information and helps event characterization.

status.label: Multiple stages
status.evidence: The October 2026 collaboration report documents Fermilab characterization data and a forthcoming SNOLAB twin. A reactor CEvNS deployment remains prospective.

timeline.event: ININ and Laguna Verde reactor-CEvNS configurations studied
Fermilab SBC-LAr10 observed first bubbles and began a calibration campaign

phases.name: SBC-LAr10 Fermilab
phases.description: 10 kg device in the MINOS underground facility; first bubble events do not by themselves establish a 40–100 eV calibrated response.

phases.name: SBC-SNOLAB
phases.description: A twin chamber for dark-matter studies; distinct from a reactor experiment.

phases.name: Reactor CEvNS configurations
phases.description: ININ 10 kg and Laguna Verde 100 kg are sensitivity-study options, not verified operating neutrino detectors.

results.summary: First bubble-nucleating events and multi-channel detector characterization were reported. No reactor-neutrino CEvNS detection is claimed by this archive.
